title: How Much Performance Marketing Costs in India, and How to Budget
excerpt: Performance marketing cost in India is ad spend plus a management fee. Here is what drives each, how agencies price it, and how to work out your own monthly budget.
author: Marketix Studio
metaTitle: How Much Performance Marketing Costs in India
metaDescription: What performance and digital marketing cost per month in India, how agencies price it, and a simple way to work out a budget for your own business.
secondaryKeywords: digital marketing cost per month in india
digital marketing cost for small business in india

paragraphs: How much performance marketing costs in India comes down to two things: the ad spend you pay Google or Meta, and the fee you pay whoever runs the campaigns. There is no fixed price. Your ad spend depends on what each lead or sale costs and how many you need, while fees are usually a retainer, a percentage of spend, or both.

This post explains what goes into the total, how digital marketing costs differ from performance marketing costs, what a small business should expect per month, how agencies price their work, and a step by step way to estimate a budget for your own business instead of relying on someone else's number.

sections.heading: Key takeaways
points: Your total performance marketing cost is ad spend plus a management fee plus supporting costs such as landing pages, creatives and tools.
Ad spend should be worked backwards from the number of leads or sales you need and what each one is likely to cost, not picked as a round number.
Agencies usually charge a fixed monthly retainer, a percentage of ad spend, or a mix, and each model suits a different stage of business.
Small businesses get more from a focused budget on one or two channels than from a thin budget spread across many.
The right budget is one your margins can support, which is why knowing your break-even cost per sale matters more than any market rate you read online.

sections.heading: How much does performance marketing cost in India?
paragraphs: Performance marketing in India costs whatever your ad spend is, plus the management fee, plus any one-time setup work. The ad spend is usually the largest part, and it is driven by your market, not by the agency.
When a client asks us for a number, we first look at the factors below, because each one moves the cost of a lead or sale up or down.
points: Competition in your category: when many businesses bid on the same searches or audiences, clicks cost more. Categories where one customer is worth a lot tend to be expensive because advertisers can afford to bid high.
Location: targeting one city or a few pin codes costs less in total than targeting the whole country, though cost per click in metros can be higher.
Channel: Google Search reaches people actively looking, so clicks often cost more but intent is stronger. Meta ads usually give cheaper reach but need better filtering to get serious leads.
Your offer and landing page: a page that converts well lowers cost per lead without touching the bid. A weak page makes every rupee of spend work less.
Volume: the more leads or orders you need each month, the more you spend, and costs can rise once you exhaust the cheapest audiences.
Scope of management: the number of platforms, campaigns, creatives and reports you need decides how much work goes into running the account.

sections.heading: How much does digital marketing cost per month?
paragraphs: Digital marketing costs more than performance marketing alone because it covers more work. Performance marketing is paid ads judged on leads and sales; digital marketing also includes SEO, social media, content, email, WhatsApp and your website.
Each piece has its own cost pattern, so it helps to separate one-time costs from monthly ones before comparing quotes.
points: Ad spend (monthly): paid directly to Google, Meta or other platforms. GST is charged on ad spend billed in India, so add it to your planning.
Ads management (monthly): the fee for planning, running and optimising campaigns.
SEO (monthly): ongoing technical fixes, content and link work. It takes months to build, so it is usually a longer commitment.
Social media management (monthly): organic posting, design and community replies, separate from paid ads.
Email and WhatsApp (monthly): platform charges plus the work of writing and setting up campaigns and automations.
Website or landing pages (mostly one-time): design and development, with smaller ongoing costs for hosting and changes.

sections.heading: What does digital marketing cost for a small business in India?
paragraphs: For a small business, digital marketing can cost very little to start if you begin with free basics and one paid channel. The mistake we see most often is spreading a small budget across five channels so that none of them gets enough data to work.

Pick the channel that matches how your customers already buy. A clinic, salon or showroom usually starts with a complete Google Business Profile, which is free, and search ads for local intent. Our [Local SEO & Google Business](/services/local-seo-gmb) work starts there for that reason. An online store usually starts with Meta ads and Google Shopping.

Your budget also needs to be large enough for the platform to learn. Meta, for example, says an ad set generally needs around 50 optimisation events within a week to exit the [learning phase](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/112167992830700). If your budget cannot produce that many results, choose an earlier event to optimise for or narrow your campaigns.

Example: a local business wants 30 enquiries a month and expects each to cost around ₹400. That suggests roughly ₹12,000 in ad spend, plus a management fee and GST. These are round illustrative numbers, not a market rate; your own costs could be lower or much higher.

sections.heading: How do agencies price performance marketing?
paragraphs: Agencies price performance marketing in one of four ways. None is automatically better; what matters is that the model matches your spend and stage.
Here is how each works side by side.
points: Fixed monthly retainer: you pay a set fee regardless of spend. Predictable and simple, but the fee does not adjust if your spend grows or shrinks sharply.
Percentage of ad spend: the fee is a share of what you spend on ads. It scales with work, but it can tempt an agency to recommend more spend than you need.
Retainer plus percentage: a base fee covers fixed work, and a smaller percentage applies above a spend threshold. Common for growing accounts.
Performance-based: you pay per lead or sale, or a bonus on results. It sounds attractive but needs clear agreement on what counts as a qualified lead, otherwise you pay for junk.

When to choose which: a retainer suits smaller, steady budgets; a percentage or hybrid suits larger accounts that will scale; performance-based deals suit businesses with clean tracking and a clear definition of a good lead.
Watch for extras: ask whether creatives, landing pages, tracking setup and reporting are included, as these often explain why two quotes look so different.

sections.heading: How to work out your own performance marketing budget
paragraphs: The most reliable way to set a budget is to start from your revenue target and work backwards. This takes ten minutes with your own sales data and gives you a number you can defend.
These are the steps we follow with clients before recommending any spend.
points: 1. Decide how many sales or customers you want from ads each month.
2. Look at your conversion rate from lead to sale. If one in ten leads buys, you need ten leads per sale.
3. Estimate a realistic cost per lead for your channel and city. Use past data if you have it, or a short test campaign if you do not.
4. Multiply leads needed by cost per lead to get monthly ad spend.
5. Check that the cost per sale stays below what you can afford to pay. Our guide on [break-even ROAS](/blog/break-even-roas-calculation) shows how to calculate that limit from your margins.
6. Add management fees, GST and any one-time setup, then run it for a fixed test period before deciding to scale or cut.

sections.heading: Example: a worked monthly budget
paragraphs: Example: a business wants 10 sales a month. One in eight leads converts, so it needs 80 leads. If a lead costs about ₹500, ad spend is roughly ₹40,000. Add a management fee and GST on top. All figures here are round numbers for illustration only.

Now check affordability. ₹40,000 for 10 sales is ₹4,000 per sale in ad spend. If the profit on one sale is more than that plus your share of fees, the budget works. If not, you need a better conversion rate, a cheaper channel or a higher-value offer before spending more.

sections.heading: Getting a realistic budget for your business
paragraphs: Any number quoted without looking at your margins, conversion rate and market is a guess. A useful budget comes from your own figures and a short test that replaces assumptions with real cost per lead.

faqs.question: Is digital marketing cost the same as performance marketing cost?
faqs.answer: No. Performance marketing cost covers paid ads and their management, measured against leads or sales. Digital marketing cost also includes SEO, social media, content, email, WhatsApp and website work, so the total is usually higher.

faqs.question: Can I run performance marketing with a small budget?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you keep it focused. Choose one channel, a tight location and a clear offer so the budget produces enough results for the platform to learn. A small budget spread across many campaigns rarely gives useful data.

faqs.question: Why do digital marketing prices vary so much between agencies?
faqs.answer: Quotes differ because scope differs. One agency may include creatives, landing pages, tracking and detailed reporting, while another quotes only campaign management. Compare what is included, not just the headline fee.

faqs.question: Is GST charged on ad spend and agency fees in India?
faqs.answer: Yes. GST applies to ad spend billed by Google and Meta to Indian advertisers, and agencies registered for GST also charge it on their fees. Include both when planning your monthly budget.

faqs.question: How long before I know if my budget is working?
faqs.answer: Give a new campaign a fixed test period, usually a few weeks, so the platforms can learn and you collect enough leads to judge quality. Judge it on cost per qualified lead and cost per sale, not on clicks or impressions.
